title: Small thefts become a habit
odia:
କଖାରୁ ଚୋର, ଲାଉ ଚୋର
ଚୋରାଉ ଚୋରାଉ ବଡ଼ା ଚୋର।
literal_meaning: A pumpkin thief, a bottle-gourd thief—stealing and stealing, a big thief.
meaning_odia: ଛୋଟ ଛୋଟ ଚୋରିକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର କରୁଥିଲେ ସେହି ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ବଡ଼ ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ଆଡ଼କୁ ନେଇଯାଇପାରେ। କଖାରୁ ଓ ଲାଉ ଚୋରିରୁ ବଡ଼ ଚୋର ହେବାର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଏହି ସତର୍କତା ରହିଛି।
explanation: The saying follows a pattern from stealing ordinary vegetables to becoming a bigger thief. Its repeated stealing and stealing makes the growth of a habit audible. The inspected source gloss supports this warning about repeated small thefts developing into more serious wrongdoing.
usage_example: Someone keeps taking small amounts from a shared fund and dismisses each incident as insignificant. The saying could warn against allowing that conduct to become routine. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: Pumpkin and bottle gourd give the warning concrete objects before the final phrase enlarges the scale. The repeated word for thief links the beginning and ending, while the repeated verb supplies the steps between them.
